summary: H.R. 9388, titled the One-Stop Pilot Program Extension Act, extends and updates the Transportation Security Administration's One Stop Security pilot program. The program allows certain passengers and their checked baggage arriving from specific foreign airports to take connecting flights in the United States without going through additional TSA security re-screening.

affected_groups.effect: They may continue on additional U.S. flights without undergoing extra TSA security re-screening, provided specific baggage and inspection criteria are met.
affected_groups.group: Air passengers arriving from participating foreign airports with connecting flights in the U.S.

affected_groups.effect: The agency continues administering the pilot program under revised security and coordination requirements through December 23, 2032.
The agency must receive and review timely baggage images prior to passenger arrival to ensure border security enforcement can be completed efficiently.

key_provisions: Extends the One Stop Security pilot program from December 23, 2028, through December 23, 2032.
Requires that passengers arriving from participating foreign airports are unable to access their checked baggage until they reach their final destination.
Requires U.S. Customs and Border Protection to receive timely images of the checked baggage prior to the passengers' arrival in the United States.
Maintains the requirement that initial checked baggage screening at participating foreign airports uses an explosives detection system under an aviation security agreement.
Specifies that baggage and passengers may skip additional TSA re-screening only if U.S. Customs and Border Protection has not identified them for further inspection.
missing_information: The specific foreign airports participating in the pilot program are not listed in the text.
The exact number of passengers affected annually is not provided.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9388, titled the One-Stop Pilot Program Extension Act, extends and updates the Transportation Security Administration's One Stop Security pilot program. The program allows certain passengers and their checked baggage arriving from specific foreign airports to take connecting flights in the United States without going through additional TSA security re-screening.
summary_detail.significance: The bill extends an existing aviation security pilot program by four years and updates operational requirements between the TSA and U.S. Customs and Border Protection for international connecting flights.
